tasks.short: Assign firefighters strategically for rescue and effective extinguishing agent application.

steps.what: Inspect the native incident map, crew status and available extinguishing resources
inputs: actual crew reports and resource status

steps.what: Assess rescue priorities and choose firefighter jobs and strategic locations
Formulate and check the final crew assignment message and radio recipient
outputs: approved final crew assignment message and recipient

steps.what: Transmit the approved final assignment to the designated firefighters by radio
inputs: approved final crew assignment message and recipient

steps.what: Confirm actual crew understanding and monitor deployment changes
inputs: actual firefighter responses and scene changes

steps.what: Write and approve the actual deployment entry with crew, location and time
Save the approved final deployment entry in the incident record

tasks.design: Configure a native {INCIDENT_SYSTEM} view of existing map, crew and resource entries. OTHER denotes that incident system and TELEPHONY the operational radio. The supervisor chooses deployment, checks the final instruction and transmits it. Actual deployment recording stays manual; its same-system save earns no saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: A supervisor may navigate separate native panels to gather an incident picture.
tasks.enabler_now: A native combined view can reduce navigation without deciding deployment.
tasks.still_hard: Dynamic rescue priorities, crew safety and effective agent placement.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor interprets the actual scene and directs people.
tasks.altitude: Incident information retrieval beside human command.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: an existing incident system may support a combined map and resource view.

assumptions: All shares are provisional. The one-unit save allocation is schema granularity, not a measured click cost; it remains fully retained. Confirm residual navigation after current native views; existing runtime gets no saving.

Dispatch and crews produce existing timestamped incident_id, crew_id, last_reported_location, crew_status and resource_status in normal operations. No new reporting is assumed. s1 retains source freshness checks; unavailable or stale fields return to manual radio verification.

s3 captures/checks final crew, job, location and recipient. Every revised instruction returns to final approval before its separate transmission. s6 retains full actual capture after acknowledgement. No automatic deployment or uncounted message occurs.
research_questions: Does the existing incident map already show the crew and resource information supervisors need?

incremental.description: Check incident view mappings and freshness labels

approvals.approved_version: s3 final crew assignment and radio recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only native view navigation changes: 15 times 30% = 4.5 hours less 1 upkeep = 3.5. Low halves this retrieval benefit: 2.25 minus 1 = 1.25. Same-system save has no benefit.

tasks.short: Communicate fire details over two-way radios.

steps.what: Gather and verify actual fire details from scene observations and crew reports
Formulate and check the complete final radio message and intended recipient
outputs: approved final fire detail message and recipient

steps.what: Transmit the approved final fire details over the two-way radio
inputs: approved final fire detail message and recipient

steps.what: Listen for actual acknowledgement and identify any message needing correction
Write and approve the actual message time, recipient and acknowledgement record
inputs: approved final fire detail message and recipient

steps.what: Save the approved final radio communication note

tasks.design: Retain radio communication. OTHER is the {INCIDENT_SYSTEM} record and existing reporting aide; TELEPHONY denotes the two-way radio. Message preparation, final check, transmission, actual acknowledgement, note writing and same-system save are separate. Assessing native aides and record templates finds no additional change under the stated existing direct-entry setup.
tasks.previous_blocker: The task depends on concise current observations and reliable radio understanding.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing radio reporting aides already structure the message; no new automation benefit is established.
tasks.still_hard: Accurate urgent communication as conditions change.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor chooses what matters and checks understanding.
tasks.altitude: Human radio communication with explicit record boundaries.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: radio communication requires current observations, recipient selection and acknowledgement; automatic transcription cannot establish those facts.

assumptions: Provisional shares are not a measured baseline. Before assigning zero, message preparation and later record writing/save were split out and native aides/templates assessed. Existing direct-entry note template has no demonstrated duplicate transcription to remove.

This instance addresses internal superiors, crew or internal dispatch. An interagency recipient outside the organisation requires act_external authority and the same final-version gate before that transmission.

s5 captures actual incident_id, message_time, recipient, transmitted_detail and acknowledgement after the exchange at full time. A changed message returns to s2 before retransmission. No new system is introduced, so no incremental upkeep is created.
unknowns: Whether actual radio notes are copied into a second system
research_questions: Is there genuine duplicate communication-note entry beyond the current native incident template?

incremental.description: No new system or upkeep; existing radio and record actions retained

approvals.approved_version: s2 complete final fire message and recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: All observation, preparation, transmission, acknowledgement and separated record actions remain fully retained; no additional change beyond existing native aides is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Lead an engine, hand, helicopter or prescribed fire crew as a working leader.

steps.what: Review current crew briefing and operational constraints in the native incident view
inputs: actual current briefing and crew assignments

steps.what: Work alongside the crew and supervise actual fire operations and crew welfare
Choose adjustments and check the final crew instruction and recipient
outputs: approved final working-crew instruction and recipient

steps.what: Deliver the approved final instruction to the working crew
inputs: approved final working-crew instruction and recipient

steps.what: Write and approve actual crew activity, changes and welfare observations
Save the approved final working-crew note

tasks.design: Configure the native {INCIDENT_SYSTEM} briefing view, denoted OTHER. Keep work, supervision, decisions and instruction delivery with the working leader. Instruction approval and delivery are separate; actual crew notes follow the work and their existing save earns no saving.
tasks.previous_blocker: Briefing details may be distributed across current incident panels.
tasks.enabler_now: A native briefing view can reduce navigation only.
tasks.still_hard: Leading while doing hazardous physical work.
tasks.human_edge: The working leader notices crew condition and changing ground conditions.
tasks.altitude: Human working leadership beside current incident information.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: native incident views can group existing briefing fields without taking operational command.

assumptions: Shares and retained effort are provisional. Credit only additional navigation reduction after existing views; if the briefing is already consolidated, no benefit is established.

Existing command staff produce current incident_id, operational_objective, assigned_crew and constraints in their normal briefing; no new upstream capture is assumed. s1 verifies currency and retains reading. Missing data uses manual briefing.

s3 captures/checks final instruction and recipient before separate delivery. s5 writes actual activity, time and observed_condition at full time. Physical tasks and monitoring remain full; same-system save remains full.
research_questions: Can a native view reduce actual briefing navigation beyond the current setup?

incremental.description: Maintain briefing view and source labels

approvals.approved_version: s3 complete final working-crew instruction and recipient

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Only briefing navigation changes: 10 times 30% = 3 hours less 1 upkeep = 2. Low halves retrieval benefit: 1.5 minus 1 = 0.5.

tasks.short: Evaluate fire size, location and condition.

steps.what: Observe the actual fire extent, location, spread and current conditions
Retrieve existing incident maps and timestamped reports in a native combined view
inputs: actual timestamped dispatch and crew reports

steps.what: Evaluate fire size, location and condition against direct observations and checked reports
Write and approve the fire assessment with time, location and uncertainties
outputs: approved final actual fire assessment record

steps.what: Save the approved final fire assessment record
inputs: approved final actual fire assessment record

tasks.design: Configure existing map and report panels in {INCIDENT_SYSTEM}, denoted OTHER. The supervisor observes and evaluates the actual fire. Report capture, assessment writing, final approval and existing same-system save remain fully retained. No model estimates spread or substitutes for scene evaluation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Existing contextual maps and reports may require repeat navigation.
tasks.enabler_now: Native views can group existing location and timestamp fields.
tasks.still_hard: Interpreting incomplete observations of a changing fire.
tasks.human_edge: The supervisor distinguishes direct observation from uncertain or stale reports.
tasks.altitude: Source retrieval alongside human fire evaluation.

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: a native incident view may group existing maps and timestamped reports.

assumptions: All allocations are provisional; validate remaining map navigation after current native functions before crediting savings. Save receives no benefit.

Dispatch and crews supply existing incident_id, reported_location, observed_time, report_author and condition_text through normal reports. No new remote observation or structured fire estimate is assumed. s2 retains reading and stale-source checking; absent data uses manual verification.
s4 captures actual assessment_time, observed_extent, location, condition and uncertainties at full time. The assessment is not an automatically issued command or uncounted dispatch.
research_questions: Do current incident panels already provide the required contextual map and reports together?

incremental.description: Check map and report source mappings

approvals.approved_version: s4 final actual fire assessment record
